Know your grades

USDA grading standard: http://meat.tamu.edu/beefgrading/

It is prime, choice, select. Prime being the best.

The grading standard has been criticized as being too small. Three catagories (there are more, but they are literally only in pet food)

The most comprehensive beef scoring is BMS (Japan) or MSA (Australia). I prefer buying off BMS scale. USDA prime- is equal to 5 on BMS. BMS goes up to 12. For a 16 oz A5 BMS 12 NY strip, you are going to spend $500/lb. I'm not fucking kidding, ribeyes and tenderloins are more even still. Less than .1% gets graded this high.

But seriously, no one has that kind of money (if you do, seriously, I want pictures if you buy one of those steaks).

You get what you pay for. I would never buy anything below choice.

Grass vs grain fed

Grass fed cows are leaner and have less fat. What does this mean? This means less marbling, less flavor. It is also healthier for your heart.

Grain fed cows, usually they are started on grass and finished on grain. This fattens the cow up which means more flavor and more marbling.

Grilling!
